resources.string: ReelGuard watches for Instagram’s share and comment sheets and closes them right away, so you cannot send reels or read comments. It only looks at screen text inside Instagram, never reads your messages, and does not use the internet.
ReelGuard is watching Instagram and closes the share sheet the moment it opens.
ReelGuard is watching Instagram and closes share and comment sheets the moment they open.
Turn ReelGuard on in Accessibility so it can close the share sheet before a reel leaves your phone.
Turn ReelGuard on in Accessibility so it can close Instagram’s share and comment sheets.
Android 13 and newer: if Android won’t let you turn it on, open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings.
Why can’t I turn it on?
One count is one share stopped before it left your phone.
One count is one comment sheet closed.
Today’s and all-time share and comment counts go back to zero. Your streak, start date, and blocking stay on.
Show a confirmation each time a sheet is closed.
Close comment sheets before you can read them.
Only windows from Instagram, Instagram Lite, and Instagram Basel are inspected.
When either sheet appears, ReelGuard presses Back.
Each blocked share or comment is counted locally. Instagram is never modified.
No internet permission, no analytics, no accounts. Counters and settings stay on this phone.
ReelGuard needs Android’s Accessibility permission to see Instagram’s share and comment sheets and close them.
Come back here to confirm the status says Active.
Android 13 and newer blocks Accessibility for apps installed outside a store. If the toggle is unavailable, open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Instagram changes its screens sometimes. If blocking stops working after an Instagram update, ReelGuard may need an update too.
